what_this_is: The SLURM memory request per model, and the ONLY place it is written down. Keyed on the canonical names in model_names.json, so all three generators ask the same question and cannot drift apart. A model with no entry here gets `default`.
why_it_is_per_model_and_not_one_number: Every row in the author's sacct sweep of 2026-09-05 that belongs to THIS study is a neural network, and there are nine of them: flexible_dnn_512_256_valprop 61.2 GB, fdnn_wide_hetero 53.4, flexible_dnn_512_256_hetero 45.9, fdnn_wide_quantile 45.8, mlp_full_vbll_valprop 43.3, dnn_full_vbll_hetero 43.3, mlp_full_vbll_hetero 43.2, dnn_full_vbll_valprop 43.0, dnn_full_vbll_threshold 42.5, mlp_full_vbll_threshold 38.9 -- the suffixes valprop, hetero, threshold and quantile are this study's own noise strategies and uncertainty heads. NOT ONE tree, kernel or deterministic model from this study appears anywhere in that sweep. The QM9 screen's completed tasks put the forests at 2.7-2.9 GB. So a single number for the whole roster was set by the networks and charged to everything.
the_floor_why: The author's rule, 2026-09-04: 'No 32gb anywhere, min 64.' Every generator refuses a request below it, by name.
scheduling: ARC nodes are 8 GB per core, measured rather than assumed by mem_per_core_mb() in KIRBy/tests/slurm_scripts/where_to_submit.sh. At 8 cores, 64G is EXACTLY that ratio, so a 64G task backfills into an ordinary slot; 96G asks for 12 cores' worth and 128G for 16. From 2026-09-07 every model on both grid pipelines is at that ratio, which is where backfill pays most -- a job at the node ratio drops into almost any gap. Only the uncertainty runs still ask 96G.

64G.why: Every model on both grid pipelines, from 2026-09-07. 64G is the author's floor, and the floor is the only reason the request is not lower: the highest MaxRSS any task in this study has ever recorded is 4.2 GB, so 64G is about fifteen times the worst case. It is also exactly the ARC nodes' 8 GB per core at 8 cores, so a task this size backfills into an ordinary slot, where 96G asks for 12 cores' worth and 128G for 16.
64G.evidence: Two readings, both taken 2026-09-07, both recorded in RERUN_PLAN.md 13.28: sacct MaxRSS over roughly 1,400 completed tasks across all seven submissions, worst peak 4.1-4.2 GB. The two records disagree by 0.1 GB over which model held it -- heteroscedastic_gp on the QM9 screen, or gauche_rbf -- and not over the size. QM9 main grid 4.0, laboratory breadth 3.9 (val_gp), everything else below 3. Earlier and consistent: QM9 screen jobs 12971601-12971619, ecfp4 2.86 GB (worst qm90_qrf 12971607_0), mhggnn 2.71 GB (worst qm90_rf 12971601_2).

96G.why: EMPTY from 2026-09-07. It held the eighteen networks and Gaussian processes now on the 64G tier, on a 61.2 GB peak that came from a different run: it is fifteen times anything this study has produced. The tier is kept rather than deleted, because `default` is still 96G so a model with no entry here lands on it, and because the uncertainty runs' floor is written against this name.
96G.what_replaced_the_61_2_GB_reading: sacct MaxRSS over roughly 1,400 completed tasks of THIS pipeline, 2026-09-07: worst peak 4.2 GB. The Gaussian processes are no longer unmeasured -- val_gp holds the laboratory breadth peak at 3.9 GB and gauche_rbf finished 4 of 18 tasks on the QM9 main grid (model_hours.json).
96G.how_to_put_a_model_back: Move its canonical name into this list and regenerate. For a job already PENDING, do it in place with `scontrol update JobId=<id> MinMemoryNode=98304`, which keeps the submit time and so the queue position.

uncertainty_runs.why: The author, 2026-09-04: 'are you sure about the memory? I swear to fucking god its different with uncertainty.' They are right, and it is not a matter of taste: a grid task fits a model once per level, while an uncertainty task fits it 1 + oof_folds times per level and holds a per-molecule uncertainty for every TRAINING molecule at every level. QRF stores per-molecule quantiles on top of that. Nothing has ever measured this pipeline -- it has not run once since the redesign -- so the tree tier is not carried over into it. Raise or lower it from a sacct reading of the first completed tasks, in place with scontrol; do not guess it twice.
uncertainty_runs.applies_to: slurm_scripts_uncertainty_rerun/generate_scripts.py only. The QM9 grid's own out-of-fold pass is inside a grid task and is NOT covered by this -- it runs on the settled pairs only, and from 2026-09-07 every grid model is on the 64G tier.
uncertainty_runs.still_stands_2026_09_07: The 4.2 GB measurement is of the two GRID pipelines. Not one uncertainty task has started, so this pipeline still has no MaxRSS of its own and keeps 96G. That is the only place a request above the floor survives.

how_to_change_one: Edit this file. All three generators read it, and a job already PENDING can be moved without losing its queue position: `scontrol update JobId=<id> MinMemoryNode=<mem>`. Never change it on what a job script REQUESTED -- that is what somebody once guessed. Only sacct MaxRSS says what a job used, and the name must be joined from the allocation row because on a step row JobName is just `batch` (RERUN_PLAN.md 13.21).
settled: 2026-09-05, by the author: 'only high-compute models need the 96G limit'. Read against the measurement of 2026-09-07, no model on either grid pipeline is high-compute by memory -- the worst is 4.2 GB -- so the 96G tier is empty and every grid model sits on the author's 64G floor. The uncertainty runs keep their own 96G floor, which is the one pipeline nothing has measured.

measured_2026_09_07.what: The first real measurement of THIS pipeline, from sacct MaxRSS over roughly 1,400 completed tasks across all seven submissions.
measured_2026_09_07.where: QM9 screen, heteroscedastic_gp. QM9 main grid 4.0, laboratory breadth 3.9 (val_gp), everything else below 3.
measured_2026_09_07.so: 64G is 15.6x the worst observed and 96G is 23.4x. The 61.2 GB figure the tiers were built on is 15x anything this study has produced -- it came from a different run and does not describe this pipeline. The tiers are NOT cut below the author's 64G floor here; what the measurement supports is moving the 96G tier DOWN to 64G, which is also exactly the nodes' 8 GB/core and so backfills where 96G waits for 12 cores' worth.
measured_2026_09_07.not_yet_measured: Written 2026-09-07 as 'gauche_rbf has never completed a task on either pipeline, and ngboost's deep run has not started'. Checked the same day and the first half is wrong: model_hours.json records gauche_rbf finishing 4 of 18 tasks on the QM9 main grid at 1.567 h, and RERUN_PLAN.md 13.28 puts a gauche_rbf peak at 4.2 GB. ngboost's deep run has still not started, and ngboost was already on the 64G tier, so it does not move either way.
measured_2026_09_07.applied: APPLIED 2026-09-07. The eighteen models on the 96G tier moved to 64G: dnn, mlp, dnn_bnn_full, dnn_bnn_last, dnn_bnn_variational, dnn_vbll, dnn_vbll_hetero, mlp_bnn_full, mlp_bnn_last, mlp_bnn_variational, mlp_vbll, mlp_vbll_hetero, dnn_bnn_full_mve, mlp_bnn_full_mve, gauche, gauche_rbf, het_gp_rbf, het_gp_tanimoto. Nothing went below the author's 64G floor and the uncertainty runs did not move. To reverse: put the names back in the 96G list, or on a pending job `scontrol update JobId=<id> MinMemoryNode=98304`.
